name: Street Luge
description: A low-profile, motorized sled ridden in a supine position, inches from the ground surface. Originally a gravity-only downhill racing vehicle, GLMZ's version adds electric thrust and magnetic ground-effect stabilization. Riders lie flat on their backs at speeds exceeding 100 km/h with nothing but a helmet and the sled's low profile protecting them. It is the most dangerous personal transport in the city, and the racing community treats its fatality rate as a feature, not a bug. You haven't lived until you've ridden a luge through the industrial district at 3 AM.
propulsion: Electric thrust, magnetic ground-effect, gravity on hills
range: 15 km powered, gravity extends range on slopes
autonomy: Manual only. You feel every crack in the road surface.
armament: None. The ground is close enough to be a weapon.
common_usage: Underground racing, extreme courier work, proving you're insane.
story_hooks: A street luge racer discovers that at certain speeds, their magnetic ground-effect system interacts with something buried under the road surface
The street luge racing circuit is a recruitment pipeline — but for what organization, nobody knows
related_entities: Kelpline Logistics HarbourSkate MX-40 Magnetic Levitation Cargo Sled
physical_description: A skeletal aluminum chassis barely two feet wide, scarred by countless asphalt impacts and patched with mismatched carbon-fiber panels. The frame sits inches above the ground, its undercarriage bristling with exposed magnetic coils and a jury-rigged electric motor that hums with an unstable whine. Scuffed grip tape covers the rider's bay where shoulders and hips lock in; brake cables run visibly along the sides, frayed where they've been hastily re-soldered.
